title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
大大能跑，
我也能跑。
（不过我还太小了，
没有大大跑得快哦。）
page_text_en:
Big Bear can run,
I can run too.
(But I'm still too small,
I can't run as fast as Big Bear.)
summary_zh: 本页展示了大熊和小刺猬在草地上奔跑的场景，小刺猬模仿大熊跑步，内心想着自己虽然能跑，但还太小，跑得不如大熊快。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
大大能跳，
我也能跳。
（大大跳得好远好远……
我呢，只能跳一小步。）
page_text_en:
Big can jump,
I can jump too.
(Big jumps so far, so far...
I, though, can only jump a little step.)
summary_zh: 大熊在草地上高高跳起，小刺猬站在石头上模仿跳跃，内心想着自己跳得不如大熊远。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
大大会荡秋千……
我也会。
（大大荡得好高好高，
都快荡到天上去了，
总有一天我也能荡到天上。
我一定能！）
page_text_en:
Big Bear can swing on the branch...
I can too.
(Big Bear swings so high, so high,
almost reaching the sky.
One day, I'll swing up to the sky too.
I can do it!)
summary_zh: 大熊在树枝上荡秋千，小刺猬在旁边模仿，内心充满信心，相信自己总有一天也能荡得很高。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
大大能爬上高高的大树……
当然啦，我也能。
（可是我用了好长好长的时间，才能爬到大大一伸手
就能到达的地方。）
page_text_en:
Big Bear can climb up the tall tree...
Of course, I can too.
(But it took me a long, long time to climb to where Big Bear can reach with just one hand.)
summary_zh: 大熊轻松爬上高高的树枝，小刺猬也在模仿攀爬，内心想着自己虽然努力，但需要花费很长时间才能到达大熊轻易就能到的地方。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
大大能看得到的地方，
我也能看得到。
（往上，再往上，哈！我到了天上。
我从来没想过自己会到达这么高的地方。
可是大大在地上，
我怎么才能下去呢？）
page_text_en:
The big one can see places,
I can see them too.
(Up, up higher, ha! I've reached the sky.
I never thought I'd get to such a high place.
But the big one is on the ground,
how can I get down?)
summary_zh: 大熊站在树干上眺望远方，小刺猬爬到高处的树枝上，内心既兴奋又担忧，虽然看到了高处的风景，却不知如何安全返回地面。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
大大会做运动……

我也能。

（大大在沙地上挖出一个大洞……

当然啦，如果我掉进大洞里，只有大大能把我弄出去。）
page_text_en:
Big Bear does exercises...

I can too.

(Big Bear digs a big hole in the sand...

Of course, if I fall into the big hole, only Big Bear can get me out.)
summary_zh: 大熊在做运动，小刺猬模仿并表达自己也能做到，但内心担忧如果掉进大熊挖的洞里，只有大熊能救自己出来。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
不过，有一个地方只有我能去，
大大可去不了。
在那里……
page_text_en:
But there's one place only I can go,
Big Bear can't reach.
There……
summary_zh: 小刺猬发现了一个只有自己能去的地方，大大熊去不了，它正爬进一片茂密的灌木丛中。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
我可以找到好多好多宝贝哦。

我可以做国王。
和大大一样，我也是第一！

大大知道我在这里
玩得很开心。
page_text_en:
I can find so many treasures.

I can be king.
Just like Big Big, I am number one too!

Big Big knows I am having fun here.
summary_zh: 小刺猬在灌木丛中发现许多宝贝，感到自豪，并想象自己能像大熊一样做国王，同时相信大熊知道它玩得很开心。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
不过，大大只能看到……

我绿色的洞穴。
我还想去海上游玩，
我好想驾着飞船在天空中自由飞行。
page_text_en:
But, Big Bear can only see...

My green burrow.
I also want to go play at sea,
I really want to fly freely in the sky in a spaceship.
summary_zh: 小刺猬在灌木丛中发现了自己的秘密洞穴，并想象着未来的冒险，如去海上游玩和驾驶飞船飞行，而大熊只能看到它所在的绿色洞穴。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
我能在空中
荡来荡去，

还能飞快地跑和大步地跳。

我在树枝上爬上爬下，
在空中滑翔，
在沙地上挖出又深又大的洞……

可是大大不在我身边……
page_text_en:
I can swing around in the air,

and run fast and take big jumps.

I can climb up and down branches,
soar through the air,
dig deep and big holes in the sand...

But Big Bear isn't by my side...
summary_zh: 小刺猬在展示自己能荡秋千、奔跑跳跃、攀爬树枝和挖洞等本领，但内心感到孤独，因为大熊不在身边。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
我一个人玩，
一点儿也不快乐……
所以……
page_text_en:
I play alone,
I'm not happy at all...
So...
summary_zh: 小刺猬独自玩耍，感到不快乐，于是开始思考接下来要做什么。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
大大做什么……
我就做什么。
page_text_en:
Big Bear does what……
I do what he does.
summary_zh: 大熊在树旁伸展身体，小刺猬站在小路上，两人分别说出‘大大做什么……’和‘我就做什么。’，表现出小刺猬对大熊的模仿与追随。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
summary_zh: 大熊和小刺猬分别在树枝上荡秋千，大熊说‘我们永远……’，小刺猬接上‘在一起！’，表达它们之间永恒的陪伴与情感联结。

title_en: If Big Can, I Can Too
page_text_ocr_zh:
小的，是美好的
艾斯苔尔（著名儿童阅读推广人）
没有跟小宝宝相处过的人，或者说，没有仔细观察过小宝宝生活的人，是体验不到刚刚开始认识这个世界的孩子的有趣。他们不只一句：“大木行，我出行”这本纽约作者，肯定是知己深深，然后这本里就长来一句“小”宝宝的小刺猬故事，知道林边去问去问，其实就是真打生活中的孩子。
树上，我们可以看到大熊正兴致勃勃地想去探险，而小熊，却紧张地看着前面的石头，犹豫着不知道自己是否能跳过去。再看的瞬间，我们就可以看到大熊在挖坑，而小熊从土里的小孔里钻出来了。这个细节，揭示出上看到小宝宝们的天性。
接下来，故事开始了。说是故事，其实呢，就是大大（大熊）跟小小（小熊）在一起做很多很多的事情。大熊能跳，小熊也能；大熊能跑，小熊也能跳；大熊能跳，小熊也能跳。但是跳的没有那么远；大熊可以抓住树枝荡得又高又远，小熊只能吊在树枝上，一脸的羡慕和无奈。故事，就这样在很多次被美丽的色彩里中徐徐展开。
我最喜欢是宝宝想要那样的场景，在广阔的草原上，只有大熊和小熊在一起，四周是绿意盎然的世界。在这样让人的眼睛都只剩下草的画面上，你会觉得，他们仿佛也慢止住了。它们和大熊一样，在那山地跑着小熊后退，长大。
当然，在看完整本日记后，我已经被知道，其实最多的，还是一本叙说友谊的书，或者是叙述友情的书。但是，阅读一本书的体验有千千万，友情或者亲情，当然是书的主题，但我觉得更愿意把这本书当成一本大人写给孩子们懂得大熊的，真的，小的，是多么美好啊；你懂，故事里的小熊，虽很小，但是也想可以找到他自己的秘密花园，有属于自己的空间的。比如说，我宁愿说这更是在写真实的小世界，虽然才不到2岁，但是他的某些表情动作，跟这只有小熊实在是太像了。小熊90%的神情，还有语言不都，经常把自己的脸蛋弄得脏兮兮的。他却说只小熊一样，有属于自己的秘密花园，哪怕是一个普普通通的干草包，也都可以认真地掏掏掏，玩上好久。那是我们，对生活中那些微小而美好的东西，早就没有了好奇和探索的兴趣。
四年了，故事里的大熊，实在有点像我们这些大人，看上去无所不能；其实大熊已经老得再体会不到那个“小”人生乐趣了。但跟刺猬大熊一样，我们还是可以蹲下身来，和“小”人儿一起感受一下。小的，是美好的。
小的能做的，我们，也能做。
page_text_en:
Small is Beautiful
Esther (Famous Children's Reading Promoter)
Those who have never interacted with babies, or who have not carefully observed baby life, cannot truly experience the charm of children just beginning to understand the world. They don't just say, "Big wood goes, I go out." This New York author must be a true soulmate, and then this book brings in a line: "small" baby hedgehog story. Asking questions by the forest edge, it's actually the real child from life.
On the tree, we can see the big bear enthusiastically wanting to go on an adventure, while the little bear nervously looks at the stone ahead, hesitating whether it can jump over. In the next moment, we can see the big bear digging a hole, and the little bear popping out from a small hole in the ground. This detail reveals the nature of the little ones we see.
Next, the story begins. Calling it a story, actually, it's about the big big (big bear) and the little little (little bear) doing many, many things together. The big bear can jump, and the little bear can too; the big bear can run, and the little bear can jump too; the big bear can jump, and the little bear can jump too. But not as far; the big bear can grab a branch and swing high and far, while the little bear can only hang onto the branch, looking envious and helpless. The story unfolds slowly in many beautiful colors.
My favorite scene is the one where babies want to be: on a vast grassland, only the big bear and the little bear are together, surrounded by a lush green world. In such a picture where your eyes are filled only with grass, you feel as if they have slowed down. They, like the big bear, run and grow in that mountain area.
Of course, after finishing the whole diary, I already know that, in fact, the most important thing is a book about friendship, or perhaps a book about friendship. But, the experience of reading a book has thousands of possibilities; friendship or family affection, of course, is the theme of the book, but I prefer to see this book as one written by adults for children to understand the big bear. Really, the small is so beautiful; you understand, the little bear in the story, though small, also wants to find his own secret garden, his own space. For example, I'd rather say this is more about the real small world, even though it's less than 2 years old, but his expressions and actions are so similar to this little bear. 90% of the little bear's expressions and language, often getting his face dirty. He says, like the little bear, he has his own secret garden, even if it's just an ordinary hay bale, he can seriously dig and play for a long time. That is us, who have long lost curiosity and interest in the small, beautiful things in life.
Four years have passed; the big bear in the story is really a bit like us adults, seeming all-powerful; in fact, the big bear is already old and can no longer experience the joy of being "small." But like the hedgehog and the big bear, we can still crouch down and experience it together with the "small" ones. Small is beautiful.
What the small can do, we can do too.
summary_zh: 本页为绘本的导读或评论页，由儿童阅读推广人艾斯苔尔撰写，回顾了大熊与小刺猬之间的互动，强调了小刺猬的探索精神与童真，并反思成人应重新感受孩童视角下的美好世界。右侧配图是一只双手抱头、表情惊讶的小熊，呼应了文本中对童真与发现的赞美。

Reflect for a moment.
In the story, the big bear
is actually a bit like us adults.
Seeming all-powerful,
we probably can no longer truly experience the joys of being small.
But just like the big bear,
we can still crouch down
and share the experience with the 'little' ones.
Small things
are beautiful.

summary_zh: 本页为绘本的导读或评论页，通过文字反思成人与孩童视角的差异，强调蹲下身来感受童真的美好，并配有大熊与小刺猬依偎的插图，呼应主题。
